primitives.verbatim_quote: If μ is a σ-finite measure on a ring R, and if μ\ is the outer measure induced by μ, then the completion of the extension of μ to S(R) is identical with μ\ on the class of all μ\-measurable sets.

The completion of μ to S(R) is shown to be equivalent to μ\ restricted to the class of μ\-measurable sets S\. This equivalence is established by proving mutual inclusion: S ⊆ S\ and S\ ⊆ S. The key step involves showing that any μ\-measurable set E with finite measure can be represented as a set in S(R) up to a null set. This relies on the existence of measurable covers and properties of outer measures. The σ-finiteness assumption ensures that the proof reduces to finite cases, leveraging the structure of S(R) and the completeness of μ\ on S\. The resulting isomorphism enables probabilistic reasoning in extended domains while preserving foundational measure-theoretic integrity.
